PullRequest.Title: Add proposed GitHub API for profile gist sharing
PullRequest.Body:
- Add the `github` proposed API: `vscode.github.getClient(sessionId, token?)` and `getAnonymousClient(token?)` return disposable clients with typed Gist operations.
- Route extension-host requests through the existing workbench GitHub service: shared-process execution on desktop and local execution on web, including the main-thread bridge for remote extension hosts.
- Migrate Configuration Editing's profile Gist upload/download, removing its Octokit, tunnel, and custom proxy stack.
- Reduce Gist contracts to the fields this consumer needs, project responses with nested `parse.copyObject` parsers, and add a default-value overload to `parse.optional`.
- Simplify the GitHub service README and remove the obsolete client inventory.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after cache removal and all three session-resolution call paths are explicit in the diff and repository code, and the export awaits them serially. Exact milliseconds vary with extension-host placement and authentication-provider latency, which is why severity is low rather than suppressing the finding.
Findings.PerformanceResource: authentication-provider session enumerations and extension-host/shared-process IPC calls
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added session selection and client acquisition run once for every profile export; total control-plane work and remote round trips grow linearly with repeated exports instead of being paid once per handler lifetime.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased latency on the profile-export critical path, particularly in remote windows
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The deleted `_octokit` promise cached both `authentication.getSession(...)` and the authenticated Octokit instance, so after the first export each later export went directly to the single Gist POST.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each `saveProfile` invocation now calls `authentication.getSession`, acquires a fresh proposed-API client, performs the POST, and immediately disposes the client. The acquisition path then resolves the same session again in `MainThreadGitHub._resolveSession` and again in `WorkbenchGitHubCredentialProvider.resolveClient` before acquiring the shared-process lease.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 25 places `authentication.getSession(...)` inside every `saveProfile` call, followed by the newly added per-call `github.getClient(...)` and `client.dispose()`; the same diff deletes the prior handler-level `_octokit` promise cache.
Findings.Title: Reuse the authenticated client across profile exports
Findings.Impact: After the first export, every additional profile export now waits for three session-resolution passes plus client lease acquisition/release before its one Gist POST; on a remote workspace these add multiple networked RPC round trips to an otherwise user-initiated serial critical path.
Findings.Evidence: `saveProfile` is awaited directly by `UserDataProfileImportExportService.doExportProfile`, so all acquisition work blocks export completion. `MainThreadGitHub.$getClient` calls `_resolveSession`, which invokes `IAuthenticationService.getSessions`; `WorkbenchGitHubService.acquireAccountApiClient` then calls `WorkbenchGitHubCredentialProvider.resolveClient`, whose `getSession` invokes `IAuthenticationService.getSessions` again. That service delegates to the authentication provider rather than caching. Configuration Editing has `main` and `browser` entries but no `extensionKind`, which is classified as a workspace extension on desktop, so these newly repeated API calls traverse the remote extension-host bridge in remote workspaces.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a handler-lifetime promise for the authenticated `GitHubClient`, as the old implementation did, and dispose it with the handler registration. Clear/reacquire it when the client reports authentication or disposal invalidation; continue passing each operation's cancellation token only to the Gist request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Export a user profile to a secret GitHub Gist
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench serializes the selected profile, invokes the Configuration Editing profile handler, selects an authentication session, acquires the proposed GitHub client, creates the Gist, and returns the link. Every added acquisition and provider lookup is awaited before the export can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the serialized profile to the workspace extension-host profile handler and return the save result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request and one response per export; request bytes scale with the single serialized profile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same profile-content-handler RPC already carried the profile into the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required and serial before export completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve GitHub sessions through the authentication API/provider, then acquire an authenticated GitHub client lease.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three provider-backed session resolutions and one proposed-client acquisition per export after the PR; before the PR there was one session lookup on the first export and none on warm exports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted `_octokit` promise retained the authenticated client and session choice for the handler lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All calls are awaited before the Gist POST; in remote workspaces the extension-side calls traverse the remote extension-host connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer the one-file create request from the extension host to the main thread and acquire/execute through the desktop shared GitHub process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extension-host call and one shared-process request per export; body bytes scale with the profile string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Octokit serialized and sent the POST directly from the extension host; no GitHub API bridge or shared-process lease was involved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Carries the full profile on the serial export path before the network POST.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST one secret Gist to GitHub.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one POST per successful export, both before and after the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same logical POST was issued by Octokit in the extension host; the PR moves execution to the workbench/shared GitHub service rather than adding another POST.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dominant remote operation required to produce the share link.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One profile body and one Gist POST per export; repeated exports control acquisition multiplicity, while profile byte size controls serialization cost. There is no collection fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The profile-handler call, session lookup, client acquisition, and POST are serial. The shared GitHub request queue governs the POST, but no batching or coalescing combines separate exports.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the PR, a handler-level promise cached the selected session and Octokit client after first use. After the PR, no handler-level authenticated-client cache remains: every export repeats session selection, main-thread session validation, credential-provider resolution, shared-process lease acquisition, and release. POST requests are not cacheable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted cache, added per-call acquisition/disposal, three traced session-enumeration paths, workspace extension placement, and serial awaits are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication-provider and remote-extension-host round-trip duration varies by deployment, and exports are user initiated rather than hot-loop operations. The repeated boundary mechanism is certain, but this variability limits the reported severity to low.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: warm exports lose the previous client cache and now repeat multiple critical-path provider/IPC acquisitions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Import a profile from a GitHub Gist link or Gist identifier
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench activates the profile handler, invokes it in the extension host, acquires an anonymous GitHub client, performs one Gist GET, transfers the projected Gist DTO, selects the first usable file, and returns that content for JSON parsing and profile application.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the extension-host profile handler and return the selected profile-content string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request and one returned content string per import.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The profile handler already ran across this boundary and returned the content string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the workbench can parse or apply the profile.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire/release an anonymous client through the main thread and desktop shared process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquisition and release per attempted handler read after the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A handler-level promise cached the anonymous Octokit object, so warm reads skipped client construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Acquisition completes before the GET can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Project every returned Gist file and transfer the DTO from the shared GitHub process through the main thread to the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One DTO per GET, containing every inline Gist file; total body is bounded at 16 MiB before parsing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Octokit parsed the GitHub response in the extension host, so unrelated Gist files did not cross the new shared-process/main-thread/extension-host bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All projected file content must arrive before the handler can select `files[0]`.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold logical GET per import; compatible warm requests may be served/coalesced by the shared REST transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One logical GET was already made directly by Octokit; the PR moves it to the shared GitHub service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before profile content is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Gist per import. The response can contain multiple files and is bounded by the GitHub transport's 16 MiB response cap; DTO mapping and IPC serialization scale with total returned inline file content, while only the first file is consumed by this handler.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Client acquisition, GET, DTO conversion, and handler return are serial. The shared transport may coalesce/cache compatible GETs, but one import does not create concurrent fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the PR, the anonymous Octokit object was cached but each import still performed a Gist GET. After the PR, anonymous client acquisition/release repeats per import; the shared transport can retain a warm REST response independently of the short-lived lease. Failures are not negatively cached by the handler.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added DTO/IPC route and per-read acquisition; lower for material user impact at normal profile sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-file Gists amplify the new IPC copies, especially with a remote extension host, but ordinary profile Gists contain one comparatively small text file and the transport rejects responses over 16 MiB.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: payload movement is bounded and normally dominated by the existing network GET, while anonymous acquisition is a low-frequency control cost closely related to the reported client-cache regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start the extension host and construct per-extension VS Code API objects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The main-thread customer module is imported with other extension-host customers, and the extension host creates a small `github` namespace object when constructing an extension's API. The delayed GitHub service, authentication lookup, shared-process lease, and network stack are not acquired until an extension calls the API.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One small namespace object and two closures per materialized extension API; one main-thread customer and two listeners per extension-host connection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous initialization only; no queues, requests, or parallel expensive work are started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The API object is retained with the extension API for its lifetime. The GitHub workbench service remains delayed and clients are explicitly lease-based.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that expensive GitHub work remains lazy; only small object/listener allocation is eager.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact module parse cost is not measured, but the changed startup work is small and does not reach subprocess, filesystem, database, IPC request, or network boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all 27 changed files and traced profile export/import through extension-host, authentication-provider, shared-process, serialization, and GitHub network boundaries. Submitted one low-severity repeated-work finding for removal of the warm authenticated-client cache. The new payload route, parser projection, cleanup ownership, API startup allocation, and request concurrency are bounded or intentional and did not independently meet the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
